# routeros_tool_sms (Resource)


## Example Usage
```terraform
resource "routeros_tool_sms" "sms" {
  allowed_number = "example"
  channel        = 1
  polling        = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `___id___` (Number) <em>Resource ID type (.id / name). This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `___path___` (String) <em>Resource path for CRUD operations. This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `___skip___` (String) <em>A set of transformations for field names. This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `allowed_number` (String) Comma separated list of phone numbers that are allowed to execute SMS commands on the router. An empty value allows any number.
- `channel` (Number) Modem channel that is used to send and receive messages.
- `polling` (Boolean) Use polling of the modem instead of unsolicited result codes. Required by modems that do not notify the router about new messages on their own.
- `port` (String) Name of the serial port or of the modem interface used for SMS, for example `serial0`. `none` disables the SMS tool.
- `receive_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the router receives and stores incoming messages in `/tool/sms/inbox`.
- `remove_sent_sms_after_send` (Boolean) Whether a message is deleted from the modem or SIM storage right after it was sent.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) Secret that a received message must start with before the router treats the rest of the message as an SMS command.
- `sim_pin` (String, Sensitive) PIN code of the SIM card.
- `sms_storage` (String) Where received messages are stored.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import
Import is supported using the following syntax:
```shell
#The ID can be found via API or the terminal
#The command for the terminal is -> :put [/tool/sms get [print show-ids]]
terraform import routeros_tool_sms.sms "*1"
```
